exposure: type of cesarean delivery (elective vs. unscheduled)
outcome: prevalence of serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC)
cohort: 280 women who underwent opportunistic salpingectomy (total or partial) as a postpartum permanent contraception procedure during cesarean delivery between 2014 and 2017.
finding: The prevalence of STIC in women undergoing postpartum salpingectomy during cesarean delivery was extremely low (0.4%), suggesting that total bilateral salpingectomy can be considered a safe and effective option for postpartum permanent contraception.
